And after these things, al-Mahdi set out for the territory of the Romans,
and he encamped by the river Pyramus in the region of Arabissus.
And his son Harun captured the fortress of Semaluos, took captives, and departed.
And in the year 1092
of the Greeks, the Arabs took captive from Ephesus about seven thousand [people],
and four thousand also died of the Arabs.
Then Emperor Leo sent an army and exiled the Orthodox Syrian people,
and settled them in Thrace.
And it is said
that this Emperor Leo also hated icons and adhered to the Orthodox like his father.
And in that same year Leo died,
and Constantine his son reigned for twenty-two years.
Because he was young when he became king,
his mother Irene administered [the realm] and was proclaimed along with him.
In the year 1094
[1094], al-Mahdi sent his son Harun against the imperial city.
And the Romans took precautions
and shut in the Arabs at the river Sangarios,
for on one side was the mountain,
and on the other side was the water.
And when the Arabs were hard pressed,
they sued for peace for three years.
And Irene, like a woman's mind, consented,
and the Arabs departed.
And after a year, Ali built al-Hadath as a city.
After al-Mahdi, Musa his son [ruled for] one year and a month and a half.
Before he became king,
that is to say, in the year 1095
[1095 {OCR: 1025}] of the Greeks (784 of our Lord?),
flying locusts came and destroyed the crops,
and laid eggs.
And they came forth, swarmed, and climbed up the walls and houses,
and entered through the windows and doors into the houses.
And even the water jars, the beds, the tables, and the basins were filled with them.
And when they entered a house from the south side,
they would go out from the north side.
And along with grass and trees, they also ate woolen garments and the clothes of human beings.
And when they had finished off the whole region of Edessa and Serugh,
they crossed over to the West.
And for three years after this severe chastisement,
there was famine in the land.
And in the year 1097
[1097], the Romans went out and devastated al-Hadath, which had recently been built by the Arabs,
and they destroyed it and entirely pulled down its walls.
And in that same year Musa died in the month of Tammuz.
After Musa, Harun al-Rashid his brother [ruled for] twenty-three years and two months.
